explain.1: Load re, Python's tool for finding patterns in text. We'll use it to find ACT: lines.
explain.4: Define the calculator tool. Nothing runs yet; it only runs when the agent asks for it.
explain.5: Go through the math one character at a time.
explain.6: Is this character a digit, a space or + - * / ( ) . ? If not, nothing else may sneak in: stop with an error.
explain.7: Not plain math: send back an error, as text.
explain.8: ** means power. A huge power could run forever, so it's blocked too.
explain.9: Not plain math: send back an error, as text.
explain.10: Try the next line. If it goes wrong (like dividing by 0), jump to except instead of crashing.
explain.11: Work out the math, and turn the answer into text.
explain.12: Something went wrong while working it out.
explain.13: Send back an error, as text, so the LLM can try again.
explain.15: Define the weather tool. Here it uses made-up weather, so it works without the internet.
explain.16: A dictionary of made-up weather: city → weather.
explain.17: Look up the city (in small letters). If it isn't there, send back an error.
explain.19: A dictionary of tools: name → function. The program finds a tool by its name.
explain.20: Find the weather tool by its name, and call it with "Kochi".
explain.23: The tool list, plus new rules: write a PLAN: first, and a new one if a step fails.
explain.31: The fake LLM's replies, written out by hand, in order.
explain.35: Define the fake LLM. Like a real one, it takes the text and gives back a reply.
explain.36: Take the first reply off the list and hand it back. It ignores the text.
explain.39: Define the loop. It takes a question, an LLM to use, and a step limit (5 unless we say otherwise).
explain.40: Start the text: the tool list at the top, then the question.
explain.41: One round each time. range(step_limit) stops after 5 rounds: that's the step limit.
explain.42: The LLM reads all the text so far and writes its reply.
explain.44: Add the reply to the text, so the LLM sees it next time.
explain.46: Yes: hand back what comes after ANSWER:. return ends the loop.
explain.47: Look for an ACT: line: a tool name, then the input in brackets.
explain.49: Then the LOOK: line says how to write it.
explain.50: Found one, but is the tool name in our dictionary?
explain.51: No such tool: the LOOK: line says so.
explain.52: Otherwise the ACT: line is fine.
explain.53: Find the tool by its name, call it with the input (without quotes), and keep the result.
explain.55: Add the LOOK: line to the text, so the LLM can read the result.
explain.56: All rounds used and no ANSWER:. Stop anyway.
explain.58: Run the agent with the fake LLM, and show its answer.
